paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's call doesn't wait for you to feel ready. Jeremiah says he is "only a child" and the LORD tells him, "Do not say, 'I am only a child.'" (Jeremiah 1:6-7) I know that excuse. When the angel showed up at my junk drawer, I tried one too, and it did NOT hold up.

So what makes a call doable? The LORD gives Jeremiah three things. He says, "I am with you to deliver you." (Jeremiah 1:8) Then He reaches out His hand and says, "Behold, I have put My words in your mouth." (Jeremiah 1:9) Jeremiah brings the mouth, friend, and the LORD brings the message.

Then the LORD says the people "will fight against you but will never overcome you, since I am with you to deliver you." (Jeremiah 1:19) Notice what He promises there. He never says it will be easy. He says He will be with Jeremiah the whole way. So when God puts a job in front of you that feels too big, don't ask if you're ready. Ask who is with you, because the same LORD who was with Jeremiah is watching over His word to accomplish it. (Jeremiah 1:12)
